document.title: [Title Excised] Planning by Usama Bin Ladin to Hijack U.S. Airplane, Successful Circumvention of Security Measures in U.S. Airport
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Central Intelligence Agency 9/11 File: Hundreds of Secret Agency Documents on Osama Bin Laden Declassified
document.note: Raw intelligence report that became the basis for the 4 Dec 1998 President's Daily Brief. Says bin Laden planned new operations against U.S. targets, the hijack plan was proceeding well, and two operatives from the U.S. team evaded security in a trial run at a New York airport. Cited in 9/11 Commission Report Chapter 4, Endnote 112.

events.description: CIA information report warns Bin Ladin is planning to hijack a U.S. aircraft; two team members evaded security in a trial run at a New York airport.
Bin Ladin hoped the hijacking would be carried out before the start of Ramadan, circa 20 December.
CIA information report (TOT 031911Z DEC 98) warning that Bin Ladin was planning new operations against U.S. targets, including an aircraft hijacking.
Two members of the operational team in the U.S. successfully evaded security checks during a trial run at a New York airport.
Bin Ladin hoped the hijacking operation would be implemented before the start of Ramadan (circa 20 December) to obtain release of Abd al-Rahman, Yousef and Odeh.

key_claims: Bin Ladin was planning new operations against U.S. targets in the near future.
The plan to hijack a U.S. aircraft was reportedly proceeding well.
Two members of the operational team in the U.S. evaded security checks in a trial run at a New York airport.
Bin Ladin hoped to carry out the operation before Ramadan, around 20 December 1998.
The operation aimed to free Omar Abdel Rahman, Ramzi Yousef and Muhammad Sadiq Odeh.
